title: Best Badminton Shuttlecocks in India (2026)
summary: Three shuttlecock picks: a Cosco hobby-grade nylon, a Yonex Mavis 350 with cap colours and a Yonex Aerosensa 30 feather. Based on maker pages and Wikipedia.
description: Helps badminton players in India compare shuttlecocks. Three picks from Cosco and Yonex, with plain notes on speed and temperature.
lead: Which shuttlecock should you buy for badminton in India? This guide looks at three. One is a Cosco Aero 500, a hobby-grade nylon shuttle. One is a Yonex Mavis 350, with cap colours for different temperatures. One is a Yonex Aerosensa 30, a feather shuttle. Everything here comes from the makers' own pages for Cosco and Yonex and from Wikipedia. The Cosco page is short, so we say where a detail is missing.
columns: How the maker grades it (speed or temperature)

picks.name: Cosco Aero 500 Nylon Shuttlecock
picks.label: Hobby-grade nylon
cells: Not stated on the page we read
Hobby grade, no speed number shown
picks.verdict: A hobby-grade nylon shuttle from Cosco. The maker's page is short and gives no pack size or speed.
paragraphs: The Cosco India website describes the Aero 500 as a high durable nylon shuttle, hobby grade, with a foam head, in yellow. That is all the maker says about it on the page we read. It gives no pack size, weight or speed number.

The same site lists the Aero 999 as a match-grade nylon shuttle with a cork base, 6 pcs in a tube. So Cosco labels the Aero 999 match grade and the Aero 500 hobby grade. In our view, hobby grade suggests casual play.
good: The maker calls it a high durable nylon shuttle
The maker says it is hobby grade; in our view that suggests casual play
The maker lists the head type and colour
not_good: The page we read does not give the pack size, weight or speed
It has a foam head, while the maker's match-grade Aero 999 lists a cork base
In our view, the hobby-grade label suggests it is not meant for serious matches

picks.name: Yonex Mavis 350 Shuttlecock
picks.label: Yonex cap-colour shuttle
cells: Green slow, blue medium, red fast
picks.verdict: A Yonex shuttlecock with cap colours graded by temperature. Yonex lists a temperature range for each cap colour.
paragraphs: Yonex's Mavis 350 page gives one tube of 6 shuttlecocks, in white or yellow. It says the Mavis series has four to five times more durability than an ordinary nylon shuttlecock, with close-to-feather flight performance. These are the maker's claims.

Yonex lists green cap as slow for 22 to 33 degrees C, blue cap as medium for 12 to 23 degrees C and red cap as fast for 0 to 13 degrees C. Yonex also says the hardness of the skirt varies depending on temperature. The page does not state the weight or any tournament approval.
good: Yonex says the Mavis series has four to five times more durability than an ordinary nylon shuttlecock
Three cap colours with temperature ranges from the maker
Yonex says the Mavis series flight performance is close to feather
The maker lists one tube of 6 shuttlecocks
not_good: The page does not state the weight or any approval for events
In our view, check the cap colour against your court temperature
The durability claim is the maker's own

picks.name: Yonex Aerosensa 30 (AS-30) Feather Shuttlecock
picks.label: Yonex feather shuttle
cells: Temperature grades 1 to 5; no speed label on the page
picks.verdict: A feather shuttle. Yonex's Aerosensa 30 page says Aerosensa shuttlecocks are the official shuttlecock for the world's leading international tournaments. The page does not state the feather type, base or weight.
paragraphs: Yonex's Aerosensa 30 page says Aerosensa shuttlecocks are the official shuttlecock for the world's leading international tournaments, and that Yonex feather shuttlecocks are precision-manufactured to ensure the correct speed, distance and stability performance. The Aerosensa 30 comes as one tube of 12 shuttlecocks, item code AS-30.

Yonex lists five temperature grades, from grade 1 at 33 degrees C and above to grade 5 at 18 degrees C and below. The ranges overlap a little on the page, for example grade 4 at 17 to 23 degrees C and grade 5 at 18 degrees C and below. Yonex also says shuttlecock performance can vary by altitude. The page does not state the feather type, the cork base, the weight or any BWF approval.
good: Yonex's page says Aerosensa shuttlecocks are the official shuttlecock for the world's leading international tournaments
The maker gives five temperature grades
Wikipedia says serious tournaments or leagues are always played using feather shuttlecocks of the highest quality
not_good: Wikipedia says feather shuttles are easily damaged and should be replaced every three or four games
The maker page does not state the feather type, cork base, weight or approval

choose.heading: Synthetic or feather
choose.text: Wikipedia says synthetic shuttles, which players often call plastics, are far more durable and typically last many matches. It says feather shuttles are easily damaged and should be replaced every three or four games. It also says serious tournaments or leagues are always played using feather shuttlecocks of the highest quality. In our view, a nylon shuttle counts as a synthetic shuttle. In our view, a synthetic shuttle is the simpler pick for casual games and practice.

choose.heading: Check which shuttle your event uses
choose.text: Wikipedia says serious tournaments or leagues are always played using feather shuttlecocks of the highest quality. Yonex's Aerosensa 30 page says Aerosensa shuttlecocks are the official shuttlecock for the world's leading international tournaments, but the page does not state any BWF approval, and the Mavis 350 page does not state any approval either. In our view, ask your event organiser which shuttle is used.

choose.heading: What the temperature ranges say
choose.text: Yonex's Mavis 350 page gives a temperature range for each cap colour: green cap for 22 to 33 degrees C, blue cap for 12 to 23 degrees C and red cap for 0 to 13 degrees C. Its Aerosensa 30 page gives five grades by temperature. Wikipedia says both humidity and height above sea level affect shuttle flight.

choose.heading: What a standard shuttle weighs
choose.text: Wikipedia says a regulation standard shuttlecock weighs around 4.75 to 5.50 g and has 16 feathers. It also says different weights of shuttles are used to compensate for local atmospheric conditions. None of the three maker pages we cite gave a weight, so we cannot compare them on this.

choose.heading: Mavis 350 colour options
choose.text: Yonex lists the Mavis 350 in white and yellow, with green, blue and red cap options.

faq.q: Should a beginner buy synthetic or feather shuttlecocks?
faq.a: Wikipedia says synthetic shuttles, which players often call plastics, are far more durable and typically last many matches, while feather shuttles are easily damaged and should be replaced every three or four games. In our view, a nylon shuttle counts as a synthetic shuttle. In our view, a synthetic shuttle is usually the simpler choice for a beginner.

faq.q: Can I use a synthetic shuttlecock in a tournament?
faq.a: Wikipedia says serious tournaments or leagues are always played using feather shuttlecocks of the highest quality. Yonex's Mavis 350 page does not state any approval for events. In our view, ask your event organiser which shuttle is used.

faq.q: What do the green, blue and red caps on the Yonex Mavis 350 mean?
faq.a: Yonex lists green cap as slow, for 22 to 33 degrees C. It lists blue cap as medium, for 12 to 23 degrees C, and red cap as fast, for 0 to 13 degrees C.

faq.q: How many shuttlecocks come in a tube?
faq.a: Yonex lists one tube of 6 for the Mavis 350 and one tube of 12 for the Aerosensa 30. Cosco lists the Aero 999 as 6 pcs in a tube. The Cosco Aero 500 page we read does not state a pack size.

faq.q: How long does a feather shuttlecock last?
faq.a: Wikipedia says feather shuttles should be replaced every three or four games, or sooner if they are damaged.
